overview_markdown:
FreeClaw is a minimal Python reimplementation of the OpenClaw personal-AI-agent concept. It connects to OpenAI-compatible chat completion endpoints — NVIDIA NIM by default, with OpenRouter and Groq also supported — and exposes the agent through a CLI chat mode or Discord bots. Configuration is environment-variable driven, with a `FREECLAW_TOOL_ROOT` constraint limiting where agent tools can operate on the filesystem.

Its standout feature is a lightweight multi-agent system: each named agent gets its own config, `.env`, memory database, persona, and workspace directory, and a single `discord` command can launch all agent bots at once. A built-in task timer (with an optional sidecar API and web UI on port 3000) runs scheduled tasks and can post summaries to Discord, giving it a semi-autonomous 'always-on' feel similar to OpenClaw's gateway model.

Compared to OpenClaw, FreeClaw trades ecosystem breadth for simplicity. There is no plugin/skills registry, no multi-channel support beyond Discord, and no documented security hardening — but the entire stack is a pip-installable Python package that a single developer can read end-to-end. With 61 stars, a 0.1.0 release, and commit activity consisting mostly of README and housekeeping changes, it is best treated as an experimental hobbyist alternative rather than a production agent platform.
